posts.alt: Aerial top-down of a Carlsbad backyard sport court beside a Spanish tile-roof home, neighboring rooftops and eucalyptus
posts.hook: A court that plays true starts long before the first tile goes down.
posts.caption:
A court that plays true starts long before the first tile goes down.

Laser-graded base. Engineered drainage so it never puddles. Shock-pad tile that's easy on the knees and consistent on the bounce. Striped for two games, bordered clean, framed in turf. That's the difference between a slab with lines painted on it and a court you'll actually use for years.

The selections:
• VersaCourt modular tile (pickleball + basketball)
• Belgard paver borders
• SYNLawn artificial turf surround
• Kichler lighting

Thinking about a court at home? DM “DESIGN”.

posts.alt: North Park 1920s craftsman bungalow with sage-green siding, compact urban courtyard with porcelain pavers and string lights
posts.hook: Small yard? Here's the material that earns its keep: porcelain pavers.
posts.caption:
Small yard? Here's the material that earns its keep: porcelain pavers.

They shrug off stains, barely fade in full sun, stay cooler underfoot than poured concrete, and the large format makes a compact space read bigger. Pair them with a living wall and a slim fire feature and a tight footprint starts living a lot larger than its square footage.

The selections:
• Belgard Urbana porcelain pavers
• Trex pergola
• Bobe water bowl
• SYNLawn turf
• Kichler lighting

Working with a smaller space? DM “DESIGN” and we'll spec it.
